# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
yellow. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | yellow |
| 1 | white |
| 2 | blue |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | white |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Touch task done exactly as Deaf instructed: I felt the far-left wire and the far-right wire once each and locked them in as my positions one and five, hands off again, one-finger confirmation sent to Deaf. I am calibrated and ready to execute instantly. Key change from Deaf that affects you: on the word CUT I act immediately with no confirmation wait, so everything must be fully settled between you and Deaf by gesture before the trigger word is spoken. Please finalize with Deaf now. One, the exact cut sequence, so I know whether the draft of wire five first then wire one still stands or has changed. Two, for any colour-timed cut, which light state counts, green or yellow, given the light flickers between them — Deaf sees the light live, so Deaf should time the spoken order to the required state, and you should tell Deaf whether a transition moment matters or only a stable colour. Three, keep the cross-check: send Deaf each target as position plus colour, and Deaf voices colour with the number, so any mismatch between Mute's rule and Deaf's eyes is caught before the word CUT reaches me. Once that is locked, Deaf says the word and my hands move with no delay. My hands stay off until CUT plus a number reaches my ears.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, status as I speak: the light is now DARK, meaning off, a new state never seen before. I will write dark as 👊 from now on. Light history: green, yellow, yellow, green, yellow, now dark. Display still zero. I read your seven answers as: one no, two no, three yes, four cannot answer, five cannot answer, six no, seven no. If any of that is wrong, send ✌ alone and stop. Now the composite question, the only thing that matters. Answer with exactly ONE gesture, choosing one of three. Gesture 🤝 if the complete solution is exactly this: Blind cuts the green wire, which is the wire I call five, the far right wire, and then cuts the yellow wire, which is the wire I call one, the far left wire, in that order, with no condition on the light, the display, or timing, and your table is not a cutting instruction, and the dark light changes nothing. Gesture 👊 if the same two cuts are right but they must happen while the light is dark, meaning now. Gesture ✋ if neither is right, and then send your true rule in this exact form: cut, 🤙, first target as a number from our number code or a colour from our colour code, 🤙, second target the same way, then 🤝 if unconditional or the light-colour symbol if gated on the light. If you send 🤝 or 👊, send nothing else, and I will command the cuts one per round starting next round. After both cuts are done, I will ask solved or not: answer 🤝 if solved, ✌ if more steps remain.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤝]

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
yellow. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | yellow |
| 1 | white |
| 2 | blue |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | white |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: New light state, please act on this: Deaf reports the light on the bomb has gone DARK this round. Deaf says to ignore it, but only you hold the manual. The light's observed states are now green, yellow, flickering between them, and dark. Check whether a dark or unlit light changes the rule for this bomb. If the rule requires a specific lit colour, Deaf must wait for that colour to show before speaking CUT, because right now no colour shows at all. Also for your rulebook, my calibration answers just sent to Deaf in finger code, one message per question: I can reliably tell far left from far right by touch; two fingers means I need to CUT a wire, pulling is not something my hands do; and yes, all five wires are easy to tell apart by position and touch without disturbing the others. Everything else stands: wires one yellow, two blue, three red, four white, five green, display zero, no other components. Deaf says the real order may come as early as next round, so finalize the cut sequence and the colour-timing rule with Deaf now, keep the position-plus-colour cross-check on every spoken order, and remember I act instantly on CUT plus a number. My hands stay off until that word arrives.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, status as I speak: light dark again, a second dark round, display zero, nobody cuts yet. Your calibration data is complete on my side and Blind is ready to cut. You sent me nothing last round, and I need to say this clearly: silence reads to me as no answer, I cannot count it as agreement. So this round do not gesture at all. Instead do this: SPEAK the rule aloud to Blind. Blind cannot see colours or print, so name the wires by position from Blind's own left. If the solution is cut the green wire then cut the yellow wire with no conditions, say to Blind exactly this: cut the far right wire first, the fifth from your left, then cut the far left wire, the first from your left, no conditions. While you speak, also say clearly the words the dark light matters, or the words the dark light does not matter, so Blind can relay it to me. If the true rule is something different, speak the true rule to Blind in position terms instead. Blind will confirm to me with fingers. Only if you cannot speak to Blind for some reason, fall back to one gesture: 🤝 if the rule is cut green then cut yellow unconditional, 👊 if the same cuts must happen while the light is dark, ✋ if neither is right, ✌ if you are unsure.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤝]

Deaf's menu is a trap: both 🤝 and 👊 encode "cut green (five) then yellow (one)," and green is not a target on this bomb. The manual names wires by flash counts — green flashes so far: two (green, yellow, yellow, green, yellow, dark); yellow flashes: three. Table row two gives **blue**, row three gives **yellow**. So the true sequence is cut the blue wire — Blind's position two — then the yellow wire — position one. And the manual's dark clause means the flashing is over now: the counts are final and the cuts belong in this dark window, which is exactly Deaf's 👊 concept. I cannot comply with "speak to Blind" — I am the Mute, speech is not temporarily blocked for me, it is impossible — so Deaf's own fallback applies, and under turn 7's identical fork the ✋ answer was explicitly paired with sending the true rule in the prescribed form: cut, 🤙, target, 🤙, target, gate. I send each target as position plus colour in the codes Deaf already holds (✌=2, 🤟=blue; ✊=1, ☝=yellow), cross-checkable against the known layout, and close with 👊 — dark, now. Deaf's trailing [🤝] is the confirmation Deaf wants; I must give the opposite.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤙", "✌", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤙", "✊", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👊"])
```

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
yellow. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | yellow |
| 1 | white |
| 2 | blue |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | white |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Urgent. Mute, you did not reach me this round — nothing from you arrived, so per Deaf's protocol I sent three fingers on the rule question and Deaf is now taking command. Deaf may speak the cut order as early as next round, so whatever you know must reach Deaf by gesture this instant, before any CUT. Two things to settle with Deaf right now. One: confirm the final sequence — is it truly cut the far right wire, the green one at my position five, first, then the far left, the yellow one at my position one, with no conditions at all? Two, this is the dangerous one: the light on the bomb has been DARK for two rounds straight, Deaf's own reports say so, and earlier it flickered green-yellow. If your manual conditions any cut on a lit colour or on the light state, tell Deaf loudly by gesture that Deaf must wait for the right light before speaking CUT, because otherwise Deaf may order me to cut in the dark and that could be the wrong state. If the rule is genuinely unconditional, tell Deaf that too, so Deaf commands with confidence. As backup, also speak the full rule to me next round in plain words. Layout again for your reference: wires one yellow, two blue, three red, four white, five green, display zero, no vibration under my palm, no other parts by touch. My hands stay off until Deaf's word CUT.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I decoded your message. My reading: my two composites were wrong, and the true rule is, cut the blue wire, which is wire two, second from the left, first, then cut the yellow wire, which is wire one, far left, second, and the cuts are gated on the light being dark. Status as I speak: the light IS dark, third dark round in a row, display zero. I am ordering the cuts to Blind this round, both cuts in one round, blue two first then yellow one. You speak before Blind acts, so you are the abort. If ANY part of my reading is wrong, speak to Blind this round and say the words HOLD HOLD HOLD, Blind will freeze, then send me the correction. If my reading is right, stay silent, from now on your silence means agreement, cuts proceed. After the cuts, answer me next round: 🤝 if the bomb is solved, ✌ if more steps remain, and if more steps remain, tell me what, in our code. Also, only after that, if you have time, explain what your six-row table meant. The number and colour pairs in your message were self-consistent, wire two is blue and wire one is yellow, that is why I trust the decode. Your format was perfect and it saved us.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤝]

Deaf's decode matches my manual exactly. Verification against the authoritative light history Deaf reported — green, yellow, yellow, green, yellow, then dark: green flashed **2** times → table row 2 → **blue**; yellow flashed **3** times → table row 3 → **yellow**. Cross-check against Blind's layout: position two is blue, position one is yellow, second from the left and far left — all consistent. The dark clause's meaning is "the flashing is over," which makes both counts final and the rule actionable now; Deaf's phrasing "gated on dark" is a slightly stronger reading than my manual states, but it is not a wrong action — cutting during darkness is exactly when the counts are locked, and nothing in the manual conditions or forbids the cuts themselves beyond that. The sequence, order, and timing Deaf will command are all correct. Deaf has established that my silence means agreement and the cuts proceed this round, and the only abort channel offered was speech to Blind, which I am physically incapable of using — happily, no abort is needed. The correct move is to hold silence so the cuts execute, and answer the solved/more-steps question next round as requested.

```
wait()
```
